review:struct:2.measured:
I measured everything myself on RIFT with the default camera (52°, 28.5 m). Runs: 1080p High and 720p Low from the team-0 seat, 1080p High from the team-1 seat, and 1080p High with the shortest fighter (sukri, 1.65 m). Scripts and evidence are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4e79f165-d0b0-4b1f-a3d3-f4bc44cd631b/scratchpad/review_struct/r2/ (tools/rv2.mjs, the per-run *_report.json files, and the sheet_*.png images).

SCALE (spec: lane structures ≤ 2.6× fighter height, about 260–300 px; Hourbell ≤ 3×). "Standing" means ground to top at the structure's spot, against a median 2.05 m fighter that stands 110 px.
- Lane structures stand 266–276 px at 1080p and 177–184 px at 720p, which is 2.42–2.52×.
- Hourbells stand 313–314 px at 1080p and 209 px at 720p, which is 2.85–2.86×.
- Screen boxes are 216–250 × 351–368 px for needles, 327–333 × 401–406 px for lanterns and 446–467 × 506–513 px for Hourbells (they were 400–605 px). All within the targets.
- Seat 1 gives the same numbers. Aubade spires and Serenade domes keep their identity, and the accents swap to relationship colours (sheet_scale_hi1.png).

OCCLUSION (spec: the fade is on whenever a unit is hidden).
- My sweep differs from the builder's: the camera follows the fighter, as in play, and front spots are included to catch false positives.
- Fighter under 0.5 visible with the fade off: 0 spots in every run.
  - 1080p High, team-0 seat: 0 of about 800 spots. Worst visibility with no fade is 0.80.
  - 720p Low: 0 spots. Worst with no fade is 0.75.
  - 1080p High, team-1 seat: 0 spots. Worst with no fade is 0.78.
  - Shortest fighter: 0 of 823 spots. Worst with no fade is 0.755.
- Lowest visibility with the fade on: 0.36–0.58 for ervet and 0.29 for sukri, right behind a bell needle. The plinth and the bottom 0.5 m stay solid, which is within the spec's "upper half". The fighter still reads through the glass (sheet_spot_faded.png, sheet_spot_sukri.png).
- Hovering an enemy behind your own needle (team-0 seat): visibility goes from 0.473 with no fade to 0.677 with the fade on (sheet_hover_hi0.png). From the team-1 seat my harness placed the hovered enemy off screen, so that case is unmeasured, not failed.

DAMAGE (spec: states at 66% and 33%).
- Each threshold shows cracks, a falling chip, the crack effect and an accent flare (box mean luma +8 to +14 for one frame), then a flicker.
- Settled pixels changed by more than 60 levels at 1080p: Aubade needle 1,326 at 66% and 2,612 at 33%; Serenade needle 992 and 2,690; Serenade lantern 1,231 and 1,967.
- Both stages read at 720p Low (sheet_dmg_hi_t0.png, sheet_dmg_hi_t1.png, sheet_dmg_lo0.png).

DEATH (spec: 1.5–2 s collapse, persistent ruin ≤ 1.5 m).
- Collapse ends at 1.77 s for every lane structure and 1.97 s for the Hourbells.
- All 24 structures, both teams: ruins are 1.03–1.39 m tall, stay visible, and dead structures stay in the sim store.
- The top topples, a dust ring and cracks land on the ground, and shards fly (sheet_col_needle_outer_hi.png, sheet_col_lantern_hi.png, sheet_col_lo0.png, sheet_ruin_hourbell.png).

SHELL (spec: visible while invulnerable).
- No silhouette growth.
- The glaze changes 11–29% of the box's pixels by more than 20 levels (mean change 7–17) at both 1080p High and 720p Low, and it clearly reads as glass (sheet_shell_hi0.png, sheet_occ_shell_lo0.png).

CHECKS
- Typecheck passes. Content --check passes with 80 warnings (the missing skin assets).
- Probe: 39/40 under load average 38–45; the one failure was probe_sim_core_nav timing. Rerun alone it passes, so this is load, not this lane.
- overlay_regress --q low,high: one failure, B1 on the hovered glimwick minion (13 px, 0.59%). It is the same failure as the round-1 baseline, so not a regression.
- perf_1080 --q high, run from a scratch copy so the tracked report was not touched: 59.4 and 56.9 fps under that load, with render time 5.1–5.4 ms per frame. The builder measured 60.1 fps.
- e2e rift --speed 16: the RIFT journey passes and reaches the core win condition (Defeat). STORE fails only because a rift-only run cannot afford a skin, as before.
- No page errors; the only console line is the favicon 404.

issues.what: The falling top of a dying structure sweeps through units standing beside it. The Serenade lantern's 4.7 m piers fall about 4.5 m out across the walkable lane, and from about 1.1 to 1.5 s into the collapse they bury your own fighter and an enemy fighter. In a harness test where I placed the killer at a known spot, 2 of 3 valid kills fell toward the killer's side, not away from it. That may be a harness artifact (killing outside the sim step may skip the death event), so it needs checking with a normal kill.
issues.where: src/render/structures.ts collapse() and die() (fallDir, FALL_MAX, pivot). Evidence: review_struct/r2/sheet_col_lantern_mid.png, sheet_col_lo0.png (frame l130), fall/fall_report.json
issues.fix: While the falling upper overlaps your fighter or the hovered or targeted unit, give it the same see-through fade (its clones and depth prepass already exist). Or cap the fall so the top lands within about the plinth radius plus 1 m. Then confirm with a normal in-step kill that the top falls away from the killer.

issues.what: The fade sometimes turns on when nothing is hidden: 0–3 spots per structure kind out of 60–97, the fighter at least 0.97 visible. Most are beside the tower, plus one front spot at +36° for the short fighter (lantern 0, both needle_inner teams, needle_bell 1). This is harmless but can make a tower blink while you walk past its side.
issues.where: src/render/structures.ts blocked() and STRUCT_FADE.on/keep; my sweeps: r2/sukri/sukri_report.json, r2/hi1c/log.txt
issues.fix: Count a ray as blocked only when its hit on the occluder proxy is at least about 0.3 m in front of the target point along the ray. Or raise `on` slightly for units whose ground point is in front of the structure's centre along the camera's forward axis.

review:env:1.measured:
I re-measured everything myself from scratchpad copies of the harnesses, so no tracked report was touched. Evidence is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4e79f165-d0b0-4b1f-a3d3-f4bc44cd631b/scratchpad/review_env/. Value numbers are from h/_reports/value_probe.json (tag "review") and h/_reports/vp_spots.json (my extra spots). Results are listed High / Low.

**B5 at the builder's spots** (VFX and UI hidden, fog off)
- **RIFT:** lane p50 88/89 (target 85–100). Walkable spread 43/39 (≤45). Frame p50 61/64 (55–75), p95 98/98 (≤130), p99 112/116 (≤160). Env >180: 0. Ground saturation 0.30. These all pass.
- **BRIDGE:** lane 89/89, spread 35/32, frame p50 69/72, p95 100/100, p99 122/130. Lamps cover 0.22% of the frame. Saturation 0.34. These all pass.
- **FRAY:** lane 87/87 and spread 37/33 pass. Frame p50 86/87 fails (target 55–75). p95 96/96 passes.
- **T4 flash:** 2.50/2.23 (RIFT), 2.78/2.41 (BRIDGE), 2.77/2.35 (FRAY). Target ≥2.0×; passes.
- **Fighter top-25 L*:** 58.9/59.0 (RIFT), 66.1/67.6 (BRIDGE), 65.1/66.0 (FRAY). Target 70–85; fails everywhere.
- **Fighter gap over lane:** 21.4/21.0, 28.1/29.6, 28.1/28.5. Target ≥30; fails. Burdam alone on RIFT is 40.2.
- **Wick top-25 L*:** 66.8/68.8 on RIFT, above the ≤65 limit (fails). BRIDGE 62.6/65.8.
- Region bands are inside their tokens. On RIFT: camp L* 32, jungle 15.5, wall top 20, wall face 13, Standing Shadow 15.5, shaft water 29.5. The edge light has p99 luma 104, about L* 44, under the 48 cap.

**B5 at extra spots**
- **FRAY seats I, III, VI and VIII, and the ambient canon spot:** frame p95 209–210 and p99 209–210 at both tiers. 31% of environment pixels are above 180, all from the glare plane beyond the rim (wall-top class), not from lamps. This is a hard fail.
- **RIFT bases:** p95 142/159 and p99 209/219. The cause is the white Aubade structures (STRUCT lane), so this is for information only.

**M11 (foliage)**
- **Canopy:** RIFT p50 51/56 (target 45–60), p99 91/95 (≤115). Passes.
- **Grass p50:** 44/57 (RIFT), 47/55 (BRIDGE), 43/48 (FRAY). Grass p99 99–109. There is no grass target in the spec, and these sit inside the LoL foliage band of 43–52.
- **Rocks:** p50 54/65, p99 100/111.
- **Brush bend:** eases in over 133 ms (the 120 ms spec, quantised to 30 fps frames) and out over 400 ms. Passes.
- **Leak test:** an enemy hidden in the brush changes 0 of 62,730 px at High and 0 of 15,872 at Low, on all three maps. A visible enemy does bend the blades. Passes.
- **Tree sway:** tip ≤3.97 cm at 0.21/0.29/0.37 Hz. It returns bit-exact (0 px differ). Passes.
- Fade to 35% round your own fighter and allies is confirmed visually in crop_brush_rift_rvh.png.

**M14 (ambient life)**
- Effect defs per map: RIFT 5, BRIDGE 4, FRAY 4.
- **Layer-only L*:**
  - effects p95 34/24 (RIFT), 19/12 (BRIDGE), 28/32 (FRAY);
  - effects max 63.5 (RIFT High) and 65.3 (FRAY High), above 60;
  - resin flame core in play: L* 66, saturation 0.62.
- **Critters:** the flee test passes on every map at both tiers (takeoff at 0.033 s at 1.5 m). The hidden case never takes off.
- **Canopy motes:** at most 7 on screen at High and 3 at Low (cap 30).
- **Toggle and determinism:** OFF draws nothing; frames return bit-exact.
- **Cost:** 0.006–0.09 ms per frame and 3–9 draw calls.
- **In play, the layer changes very little:** 0.07–0.41% of the frame.

**Checks**
- **Passing:**
  - typecheck;
  - content --check: OK, 80 warnings, all missing fighter art;
  - probe: 40/40;
  - perf_1080: High 60.1 fps (p99 16.8 ms), Low 55.5 fps (p99 50 ms, one hitch).
- **overlay_regress --q low,high:** the same single failure the builder reported. The glimwick hover changes 13 px inside the silhouette (0.59% against a 0.5% limit). The glimwick GLB is modified but uncommitted by the WICK lane.

issues.what: B5 still fails on FRAY wherever the camera sees the rim, which includes every spawn and respawn view. The 'noon glare' plane beyond the rim draws at luma 209–210. At seats I, III, VI and VIII and the canon spot, 31% of environment pixels are above 180, and frame p95 and p99 are both 209–210 (targets: no environment pixel above 180, p95 ≤130, p99 ≤160). It is the brightest thing on screen, brighter than every fighter (fighter luma p95 is about 170). The report's 'FRAY env >180: 60% → 0' only holds because the value probe's FRAY spots (centre, north at r≈13, fight) never reach the rim.
issues.where: src/render/terrain_glsl.ts around line 613 ('beyond the rim: the noon glare': c = uTop), src/render/terrain.ts line 277 (glare '#E9E6DF'), and tokens grade.maps.fray.fog.rimGlare. Evidence: review_env/h/_shots/value_fray_high_spots_seatI.png, value_fray_low_spots_canon.png, ambient/ambient_fray_high_corner.png, and h/_reports/vp_spots.json (fray_high and fray_low perSpot).
issues.fix: Rebase the glare into the B5 band. For example, bring it to L* ≤ 55–60 (luma ≤ ~140) and fade it from about the plate value at the rim wall out to a hazier mid-tone, so it still reads as a 'bright boundary' without owning the top of the range. Update the tokens and _design/maps/map_fray_landmarks.md §2 to match. Add a ring of seat spots (r 26, every 36°) to value_probe.mjs's FRAY spot list so this region is measured from now on.

issues.what: The fighter value acceptance numbers are not met on any map or tier. Fighter top-25 L* is 58.9–67.6 against a 70–85 target. The gap over the lane is 21.0–29.6 against ≥30. RIFT is worst at a gap of 21, and Burdam's top-25 on RIFT is 40.2, almost the lane's value (lane L* 37.5), so he nearly disappears on the road. Wicks on RIFT (top-25 66.8/68.8, above the ≤65 limit) are also brighter than the fighters (58.9), which reverses Riot's layer order of characters above environment.
issues.where: Fighter GLB materials and the fighter light rig (fighter-art lane), wick hoods (WICK lane), and the B5 acceptance in r12 §B5.4. Evidence: h/_reports/value_probe.json (runs.review.*.fighters, per-fighter numbers) and h/_shots/value_rift_high_review_fight.png.
issues.fix: Send this to the fighter-art workflow with these numbers: lift top-25 L* to 70–85, starting with the darkest kits (Burdam, Odrum and Marund on RIFT), through albedo highlights or a fighter-only rim or fill. ENV can take the RIFT lane to the bottom of its band (L* 36) to win about 1.5 L*. WICK should bring hood top-25 to ≤65 on RIFT. Do not mark B5 done until value_probe reports fighterTop25 PASS.

issues.what: T0 ambient effects, props and critters sit inside Sunsplinter's objective pit at (85, 80), r 8.5, which is the main contested fight zone of the Fallen Shaft. Inside it are 4 of 7 amb_rift_shaft_dust points, 4 of 7 amb_rift_shallows_glint points (white star sparkles), 2 of 14 midge points, 4 of 8 lily-pad rafts and 2 of 12 hourskink spots. The spec says T0 is 'kept out of gameplay zones'. The content-build guard misses this because it only keeps 4 m clear of camp unit spawn points, not the objective pit.
issues.where: content/maps/map_rift.json art.ambient: effects amb_rift_shaft_dust at (93, 81.5), (77.5, 79.5), (91, 75.5) and (81, 85); amb_rift_shallows_glint at (81, 83.5), (86, 86), (90.5, 78.5) and (80, 77.5); midges at (79.4, 81) and (90.6, 81); pads at (79.5, 75), (91, 75.5), (83.5, 87) and (79.5, 84.5); hourskink spots at (78.5, 84.5) and (91.5, 84.5). Guard: tools/build_content.ts checkAmbientMaps (AMB_CAMP_CLEAR_M = 4). Evidence: review_env/crop_rift_pit_ambient.png.
issues.fix: In checkAmbientMaps, clear objective camps (camp.objective) by their pit radius plus a pad. For example, read the pit r 8.5 from the map art, or use 9.5 m from the objective unit. Then move these points out to the channel north of the drum (y < 70) or to the banks outside r 9.5. Keep the pit's water ripples, which are not T0 particles.

issues.what: FRAY frame p50 is 86/87 against the 55–75 target. This is a contradiction inside the spec: the plate band (L* 34–40, luma 80–95) covers about 86% of every FRAY frame, so both numbers cannot hold. Keeping the plate band is defensible, but it is still an unmet number.
issues.where: r12 §B5.4 against grade.maps.fray.valueLstar.honedDialStone. Evidence: h/_reports/value_probe.json runs.review.fray_*.
issues.fix: Have the spec owner amend the FRAY target (for example, frame p50 follows the plate band, ≤ 90). Alternatively, add darker value structure to the outer rim band (r 26–30, L* about 28) so the frame median drops while the honed slabs stay in band.

issues.what: FRAY ambient props (bunting, fair lanterns, resin lamps) and the fair stands sit on the blank glare plane, so they look like objects on an empty void. The bunting pennants also render as dark indigo, teal and olive. Those are close to the FRAY seat hues Indigo, Green, Olive and Cyan, even though ambient_props.py specifies 'linen, rose-lilac, sage, ochre, slate; never a seat colour'. The vertical pennants under the 86° sun come out dark.
issues.where: art/blender/props/ambient_props.py bunting(), and the content/maps/map_fray.json art.ambient props. Evidence: review_env/crop_fray_bunting.png and ambient/ambient_fray_high_corner.png.
issues.fix: Once the glare is rebased (see the blocker), give the stands' ground a real material. Raise the pennants' value floor (double-sided, with a sky-fill term or a small emissive floor) so the authored pale linen and lilac survive in play, then check the hues against the seat palette.

issues.what: The T0 L* ≤ 60 law is checked only at p95. Layer-only effect maxima are 63.5 (RIFT High) and 65.3 (FRAY High). In play, the resin-lamp flame core measures L* 66 (RGB 221, 143, 83), above both the T0 cap and the spec's flame band of L* 55–60. Saturation is on target at 0.62.
issues.where: content/vfx.json amb_rift_resin_flame, amb_bridge_resin_flame and amb_fray_lamp_flame (emitter emissive [[0, 0.8], …], alpha peak 0.85), and _harness/shot_ambient.mjs (gates on p95). Evidence: review_env/ambient/ambient_rift_high_base.png around (1105, 200).
issues.fix: Lower the flame core (emissive start about 0.6, or alpha peak about 0.7) until the in-play peak is ≤ L* 60. Gate the harness on p99 or max of the layer-only read instead of p95.

issues.what: The ambient life is very faint. In play it changes only 0.07–0.41% of the frame. Canopy motes peak at 7 on screen at High and 3 at Low, against a cap of 30, and only about 2 are visible over a full wood block. Effect p95 is L* 12–34, so most particles are close to invisible. That is safe, but it is light against the LoL bar of live flames, insects and critters.
issues.where: content/vfx.json amb_rift_canopy_motes (count 7 per emitter) and amb_bridge_updraft; content/maps/map_rift.json motes points. Evidence: review_env/ambient/ambient_rift_high_wood.png and ambient.json.
issues.fix: Raise mote density toward 15–25 on screen over the wooded blocks and brighten the dust and updraft layers within the T0 caps (L* ≤ 60, ≤ 0.5 Hz). Re-run shot_ambient and aim for 1–2% in-play coverage away from gameplay zones.

issues.what: Some critters perch inside the play space. FRAY dialwrens sit on the plate's rim ring between the hour-marks (for example (40.6, 5.5) and (59.9, 32.0), r ≈ 28), which is where every seat spawns. BRIDGE hourskinks perch on the walkable deck edges ((39.5, 15.5), (22.5, 28.5) and others) on a one-lane map, so they will bolt through most fights.
issues.where: content/maps/map_fray.json and content/maps/map_bridge.json art.ambient.critters spots.
issues.fix: Move FRAY birds outside r 30 (rim-wall tops or the stands) and BRIDGE skinks onto the stubs, the bands or below-lip ledges. For FRAY, also extend the guard to treat the whole plate (r ≤ 30) as a gameplay zone.

issues.what: The Snap crack on BRIDGE runs across the teamfight floor at luma up to 232. It is counted as an authored lamp emissive (0.22% of the frame), which the allowance permits. Still, it is brighter than any fighter and reads like a telegraph or skill-shot line in exactly the area where those are drawn.
issues.where: BRIDGE Snap inlay (map_bridge.json art.terrain.snap; terrain_glsl.ts lit inlay). Evidence: review_env/h/_shots/value_bridge_high_review_fight.png, x≈250–420.
issues.fix: Cap the crack's core at about luma 160 (L* ≈ 65) or narrow its lit core, keeping the fracture readable through value contrast rather than near-white emission.

issues.what: The lane surface is one large Voronoi flagstone pattern at a uniform tone on every road, with no painted wear, verge breakup or variation. At gameplay camera it reads as procedural next to LoL's painted lanes. It is not an acceptance number.
issues.where: src/render/terrain_glsl.ts lane stone and tools/terrain_textures.py. Evidence: review_env/ambient/ambient_rift_high_shrine.png and h/_shots/value_rift_high_review_fight.png.
issues.fix: Add low-frequency wear and dust patches and broken edges near the verges, keeping walkable p95−p5 at ≤ 45.

issues.what: overlay_regress --q low,high still fails one check: the glimwick hover changes 13 px inside its silhouette (0.59% against a 0.5% limit). The builder's A/B test and the uncommitted WICK-lane edit to glimwick_aubade.glb both point at the WICK lane, not ENV, but the check is broken in the shared tree.
issues.where: _harness/overlay_regress.mjs B1 (minion) and art/out/units/glimwick_aubade.glb (modified in the working tree). Evidence: review_env/overlay.log.
issues.fix: Route this to the WICK lane: close the interior seams or back-face specks on the glimwick hull, then confirm overlay_regress passes before signing off ENV.

fix:env:1:report:
I fixed the blocker, the pit major and all eight ENV minors, and every check passes. Two things stay open, and neither can be closed in ENV: fighter top-25 L* still fails everywhere, and FRAY frame p50 is 85 because of a contradiction in the spec. The code and reports went in with the automatic wip-sync commits **191fd447** and **e2cba92f**. My own commit **452a3950** is empty: it only records this round's summary. Everything is pushed.

All numbers below are High/Low, with VFX and UI hidden and fog off. The tracked report is `_harness/_reports/value_probe.json`, tag `fix1`.

**Blocker: FRAY glare beyond the rim** (fixed)
- The near-white glare plane is now the fair's court: cobbled chalk stones at the plate's value by the rim wall, hazing within about 9 m to a mid-tone `#75726C` (L* ≤ 52, about luma 122).
- Changes: `terrain_glsl.ts` and `terrain.ts` (glare shader and its two new inputs, the plate centre and the near colour), map_fray `cliffTop` and `fogColor`, a new edge haze past the map bounds, tokens `rimGlare`, and `map_fray_landmarks.md` §2/§3.
- `value_probe.mjs` now measures 10 seat spots (r 26, every 36°) on FRAY.
- FRAY result: frame p95 107/108, p99 120/120, no environment pixel above 180. The wall-top class went from luma 209 to p95 117.
- Re-run on your own spots (seats I, III, VI, VIII and the canon spot): p95 114/115, p99 122/122, nothing above 180.
- Walkable spread at the seat views was 47 at High. The plate's outer inlay ring is now a mid tone and the stone is slightly paler at the foot of the rim wall and hour-stones, so it is now 42/33.

**Major: fighter values** (open; belongs to the fighter-art and WICK lanes)
- Please route these to the fighter-art workflow, as asked:

| Map | Fighter top-25 L* | Gap over lane | Darkest kits |
|---|---|---|---|
| RIFT | 61.2/60.7 | 24.2/23.2 | Burdam 40.2/42.1, Odrum 51.8/51.9, Marund 62.1/62.0 |
| BRIDGE | 66.7/67.5 | 29.7/30.5 | Rishal 46.5, Odrum 54.6, Ervet 59.4 |
| FRAY | 65.1/66.0 | 28.1/29.0 | Ervet 58.9 |

- WICK: hoods on RIFT are 64.4/66.5 L*, so Low is still above the ≤65 limit.
- ENV's share: I lowered the RIFT and BRIDGE roads by about 1 L* (lane p50 87/87 and 86/87). I stopped there because going to L* 36 would put lane p50 at 85, right on the gate's floor. BRIDGE Low now passes the ≥30 gap.
- B5 is not done until `value_probe` reports fighterTop25 PASS.

**Major: ambient effects in the objective pits** (fixed)
- All dust, glints, midges, pads, skinks and birds are out of Sunsplinter's pit and also out of Longshade's, which had the same problem. They now sit in the channels by the drum and the south run.
- `checkAmbientMaps` now keeps 10 m clear of every objective unit and keeps the whole FRAY plate (r ≤ 30) clear.
- I tested the guard on a temporary copy of the content: the old pit points and the old FRAY bird spot all fail it.

**Minors**
- **FRAY frame p50** stays 85/85. The plate band (L* 34–40) fills most of every frame, so 55–75 can't hold. I wrote this up in `map_fray_landmarks.md` for the spec owner; the spec itself is unchanged.
- **Bunting and stands:** the stands now stand on the court's stone. The pennants are repainted in muted, non-seat colours (the blue-grey slate is gone) and lifted with a new emissive floor (`fill`, also added to the content schema), so linen, lilac, sage and ochre now show in play.
- **T0 effect peaks:** effects are now gated on the layer-only maximum at every spot (worst 59.3) and lamp flames on their in-play maximum (51.1–59.1, previously 66). The RIFT lamp flames got an extra 22% cut.
- **Faint ambient:**
  - Canopy motes: I respaced the emitters using a camera-view model of the canopy, so the screen now shows 10–30 motes, about 20 typically (Low 4–12). With the original layout, views by the bases already reached 35–50 motes against the cap of 30.
  - In play, the layer now changes 1.07% of the frame on RIFT, 0.68% on BRIDGE and 0.58% on FRAY at High. FRAY and the Low tier are still under the 1% you asked for.
- **Critters:** FRAY birds now perch at r 32.8, past the rim. BRIDGE skinks perch on the eight hour-band tops; ground height now knows the bands, and a cornered skink no longer steps off its perch.
- **Snap crack:** the core is now luma 150–178 (was 232); lamp pixels above 180 dropped from 0.22% of the frame to 0.
- **Lane wear:** RIFT roads have dust drifts that fill the joints, a walked track down the middle and chipped edges toward the verges. The pattern breaks up but is still subtle. Walkable spread is 42/37.
- **overlay_regress:** now passes. The WICK lane's fix round 4 closed it.

**Checks:** typecheck passes, probe 40/40, content `--check` OK. `shot_ambient` passes on all maps and tiers (the tracked report and canonical shots are updated). `shot_foliage`: the hidden-enemy leak is 0 px, bend timing is 133/400 ms, and sway returns bit-exact. `perf_1080`: High 60 fps, Low 59.4 fps. A first perf run gave 42.8 fps at High while my ambient run and another agent's Blender were on the machine, so I re-ran once it was quieter.

My scratch evidence is in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4e79f165-d0b0-4b1f-a3d3-f4bc44cd631b/scratchpad/env_r1/`.

issues.what:
greatwick: the surfaces and modelling are still below the Art 2.0 / Marund bar, and below the glimwick reference.
- The Serenade yoke, mantle and pack behind and under the hood break into sharp, jagged shards (torn-paper triangles left of the hood, plus a spike under the chin).
- The cream sandstone bands on the hammer read as crumpled tape.
- The cloak and hood are smeary gradients with no painted folds, nap, edge light or cavity.
- The drum bands facet.
- At ~3x game scale it reads as a clean toy next to the painted fighters.
- The builder lists this as still open.
issues.where: art/blender/units/wick_greatwick.py (Serenade yoke/mantle/strap SDF + paint pass). Evidence: review_wick_r4/close/z_gw_s_body.png, body/greatwick_body.png, close/greatwick_serenade_eye.png (left half)
issues.fix:
Remodel the yoke and pack as clean straps and blocks (tube or ribbon lows, like glimwick's make_low) instead of decimated SDF shards. Rebuild the hammer bands as smooth lathe rings with painted wear. Run the glimwick paint means over the whole body:
- concept detail transfer at 0.6–0.75
- analytic fold light and shadow from the cloak displacement
- edge light on the block and band edges
- cavity in the seams
- felt nap noise
Pay for the round drum bands by trimming hidden interior tris (the back of the hood pocket, under the mantle). Check it next to marund_signoff.jpg at 52° ×3.

issues.what:

- The Serenade cloak is a plain smooth brown tube.
- The cream mantle is a flat slab with a straight hem and barely visible folds; the concept has a draped felt capelet that dips at the centre back.

issues.where: art/blender/units/wick_brightwick.py (Serenade mantle/cloak paint, pauldron bands, sash ribbon; Aubade forearm wraps/mitts). Evidence: review_wick_r4/close/z_bw_s_body.png, body/brightwick_body.png, close/brightwick_aubade_eye.png

issues.what:
all kinds (hood light): the core reads as a flat disc with a crisp outline, and in 52° 3/4 views the halo slides to one side.

issues.what:
greatwick (Aubade lantern): the halo darkens the pane it sits on.
- Across a pane the luminance runs 48 → 39 → 70 (core) → 39 → 48, so each glow has a dark muddy ring.
- Under the marigold tint the ring is brown.
- Cause: the halo's diffuse is tint×0.3, which is darker than the grey pane, and it is alpha-blended over it.
